Section 3 Epidemic Disease Act was registered at PS Lodhi Colony. Police investigated the matter and filed chargesheet before concerned Criminal Court and DAR was filed before this Tribunal.

insurance company filed its reply denying its liability to compensate the petitioner on the ground that the offending vehicle was being plied in violation of the permit as per which the offending vehicle was only allowed to be use as a light goods carriage vehicle. It is further pleaded that even the injured Vidhan Biswas was found to be under influence of alcohol. It is pleaded that since the offending vehicle could be used only as a light goods carriage vehicle, petitioner was an unauthorized /gratuitous passenger along with 13 other persons, all of whom were it violation of the Covid-19 pandemic (DDMA guidelines) guidelines and thus not entitled to compensation. It is further pleaded that there is a possibility that the offending vehicle may have been planted to raise a false claim. It is however not denied that the offending vehicle was duly insured with respondent no.3 vide policy no.
RL2012070054 for the period from 07.12.2020 to 06.12.2021. Digitally signed CHARU by CHARU GUPTA GUPTA 2024.10.21 Date:

2 5. From the pleadings of parties, the following issues were framed on 17.01.2023. 
1) Whether the injured suffered injuries in a road traffic accident on 07.11.2021 due to rash and negligent driving of vehicle no. DL-1AE-4509 (Eicher Canter) being driven by R1, owned by R-2 and insured with R3? OPP. 
2) Whether the petitioner is entitled to any compensation, if so, to what extent and from whom ? OPP. 
3) Relief. 
6. In order to prove his claim, petitioner/Vidhan Biswas examined himself as PW-1. He relied upon his evidence by way of affidavit as Ex.PW1/A wherein he reiterated the factum and manner of the accident. He deposed that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of respondent no.1. He further relied upon his MLC prepared at AIIMS Trauma Center as de exhibited and marked as Mark A, original discharge summary as Ex.PW1/2, his medical treatment records as Ex.PW1/3(colly), original medical bills as Ex.PW1/4(colly), his Adhar Card as mark B, his PAN card Mark C and copy of his 10 th class marksheet as Mark D. He deposed that on account of being bedridden for about 5 month due to the accident, he had to incur medical expenditure of Rs.10,000/-, Rs.25,000/- towards special diet and Rs.30,000/- towards conveyance. He deposed that at the time of the accident he was 26 years of age and was doing a private job in Delhi and earning Rs.35,000/- to 36,000/- per month. Due to the accident, he lost his job and earnings. PW-1 was duly cross examined by Ld. Counsel for respondent no.1 and Digitally signed CHARU by CHARU GUPTA GUPTA 2024.10.21 Date:

RW1 Akendra Kumar examined himself his evidence by way of affidavit Ex.R1W1/A. In his examination in chief, he stated that the offending vehicle was not involved in the alleged accident. 
He denied any rash or negligent act on his part in driving of the offending vehicle. He stated that the petitioner/victims have falsely implicated him and that FIR no. 206/21 has been lodged with a motive to extort money from the respondents. He stated that none of the alleged victims were travelling in the offending vehicle. He relied upon his identity card as Ex.R1W1/1. He was duly cross examined by Ld. Counsel for insurance company. Such cross examination was adopted by ld.
Counsel for petitioners. 
8. In respondent evidence, the owner of the offending vehicle /respondent no.2 also examined himself as RW2/Sh. Bhanu Prakash Sharma. He relied upon his evidence by way of affidavit Ex.R2WA and his identity card as Ex.R2W2/1. RW2 also denied involvement of the offending vehicle in the alleged accident and pleaded the FIR to be false and concocted. He asserted that the Vidhan Biswas (Dar) vs Akendra Kumar (206/21,Lc) on 21 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/62741107/
3 liability to pay compensation, if any, lies upon the insurance company with which his vehicle was insured. 
9. Insurance company /respondent no.3 also examined its witness Sh. Parth Arya as R3W1. R3W1 relied upon his evidence Digitally signed CHARU by CHARU GUPTA GUPTA 04:24:39 Date:
2024.10.21 +0530 MACT No. 326/22 Vidhan Biswas vs. Akendra & 0rs. Page no. 5 of 25(ss) by way of affidavit Ex.R3W1/1 wherein he testified that as per the Registration Certificate, the offending vehicle was a light goods vehicle with a seating capacity of 3 persons. It is pleaded that the said vehicle was being used for transportation of passengers, beyond its permitted capacity, in violation of the permit. He testified that since the respondent no.1 and 2 committed breach of the terms and conditions of the insurance policy by violating the RC and permit, the insurance company is not liable to compensate the petitioners. He relied upon his authority letter as Ex.R3W1/1, attested copy of the insurance policy as Ex.R3W1/3 and DAR /FIR /chargesheet/RC/Route Permit as already Ex.PW1/6 (colly). He was duly cross examined by Ld. Counsel for respondent no.1 and 2.
10. Final arguments in detail were addressed by learned counsel for the petitioners/victims and counsel for all the respondents. 
It has been argued on behalf of the petitioner that since petitioner has suffered injury on account of accident that is proved to have occurred due to rash and negligent driving by respondent no.1,
respondent no.3, with which the offending vehicle was insured, may be directed to compensate the petitioner. 
On the other hand, it is argued by respondent no.1 and 2 that the petitioner has failed to prove rash and negligent driving by respondent no.1 or the involvement of the vehicle in the alleged accident. It is further argued that even if the accident is assumed to be proved, it is respondent no.3 which is liable to Digitally signed CHARU by CHARU GUPTA GUPTA 2024.10.21 Date:
MACT No. 326/22 Vidhan Biswas vs. Akendra & 0rs. Page no. 6 of 04:25:11 25(ss)
+0530 compensate the petitioner. It is argued on behalf of respondent no.3 that the petitioner/victims were traveling in the offending vehicle as unauthorized and gratuitous passengers since the offending vehicle was a goods carriage vehicle. It is argued that the offending vehicle was insured as a goods carriage vehicle and could not carry any passenger except for the driver and owner of the goods. It is further argued that the insured i.e. respondent no.2 has further violated the condition of RC which permitted a maximum of 3 persons to be seated in the offending vehicle. It is argued that as there is a clear breach of the terms and condition of the insurance policy, insurance company is not liable to compensate the victims. 
11. Now, on the basis of material on record, evidence adduced and arguments addressed, issue wise findings are as under :
Whether the injured suffered injuries in a road traffic accident on 07.11.2021 due to rash and negligent driving of vehicle no. DL-1AE-4509 (Eicher Canter) being driven Vidhan Biswas (Dar) vs Akendra Kumar (206/21,Lc) on 21 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/62741107/
4 by R1, owned by R-2 and insured with R3? OPP . 
12. Before proceeding to decide the above issue, it is apposite to note that as a settled principle of law, proceedings under The Motor Vehicle Act are not considered akin to the proceedings in a civil suit and hence strict rules of evidence are not applicable. Reliance is placed upon decision in Bimla Devi & ors. vs. Himachal Road Transport Corporation & ors. (2009) 13 SC 535, in Parmeshwari vs.
Amir Chand & ors., 2011 (1) SCR 1096 and Digitally signed by CHARU CHARU GUPTA GUPTA Date:
2024.10.21 04:25:16 +0530 MACT No. 326/22 Vidhan Biswas vs. Akendra & 0rs.
Page no. 7 of 25(ss) National Insurance Company Ltd. vs. Pushpa Rana, 2009 ACJ 287, wherein it has been held that the negligence has to be decided on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities and a holistic view has to be taken.
13. In the present case, the injured /petitioner has specifically deposed about accident dated 07.11.2021. He has categorically stated that at the time of the accident, offending vehicle bearing no.
DL-1LAE-4509 was being driven by Respondent no. 1 in a rash and negligent manner. He has deposed that the driver of the offending vehicle deliberately ignored the warnings to be slow and careful. It is due to his rash and negligent driving that the offending vehicle overturned with the sudden and forceful impact causing injuries to its passengers and death of one of them. 
14. In the present case, the Tribunal takes judicial notice of the fact that a common evidence has been recorded by one single Local Commissioner in all the 13 connected matters. It is a matter of record that injured victims namely Vishal Majumdar, Deepak Das and Ganesh Das have also been examined as eye witnesses /victims in all the cases. Apart from the testimony of the petitioner,
testimony of other victims regarding the factum of accident, manner of accident, rash and negligent driving by respondent no.1, is coherent and suffers from no apparent discrepancy. All the victims have corroborated that despite being repeatedly cautioned, driver of the offending vehicle continued to driver at a high speed, in a rash and negligent manner and lost control/balance while taking a sharp turn. Page no. 8 of 25(ss) Though the respondents have denied that the offending vehicle was hired by Ganesh Das or anyone else for the purpose of idol immersion, reporting of the matter immediately to the police on the same date sizure of the vehicle by the police on the same date, preparation of MLCs of the victims as well as respondent no.1 at the same time and in the same hospital as well as filing of chargesheet by the investigating officer after thorough investigation of the accident, supports the plea of the petitioners. It has been held in National Insurance Co. Vs. Pushpa Rana 2009 ACJ 287 Delhi that the completion of investigation and filing of chargesheet are sufficient proof of negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle. 
It is further observed that though respondent no.1 and 2 denied occurrence of the accident in their evidence as R1W1 and R2W1 respectively, during cross examination Vidhan Biswas (Dar) vs Akendra Kumar (206/21,Lc) on 21 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/62741107/
5 of R1W1 (i.e. respondent no.1/driver), such witness admitted being driver of the offending vehicle on the date of accident. Though he volunteered to state that he was not driving the said vehicle at the time of the alleged accident, he admitted that at around 02:00 p.m he took the vehicle from Lodhi Road Bus Stand and was going towards Chhatarpur. On further cross-examination he stated that he was not injured in the said accident and also admitted that his medical record of treatment was prepared at AIIMS Hospital on the date of accident. The admission on the part of respondent no.1 regarding being driver of the offending vehicle at the relevant time and the fact that he was taken to AIIMS Hospital for treatment on the date of accident, proves the factum of occurrence of the accident. Since no evidence has been led by the Digitally signed CHARU by CHARU GUPTA GUPTA 04:25:26 Date:

Page no. 9 of 25(ss) respondents to show that respondent no.1 was not driving the offending vehicle rashly or negligently, by preponderance of probabilities, claim of the victims that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of respondent no.1,
stands proved. 
It has also been pleaded on behalf of the insurance company that since the victim was under the influence of alcohol and was out on the streets in violation of the Covid-19 Pandemic guidelines, deduction in respect of contributory negligence also be made. 
There is nothing in the MLC of the petitioner to show that he was intoxicated. In the considered opinion of this Tribunal, intoxication by the victim (mere passenger in a vehicle) or breach of pandemic protocol issued only for safety from the pandemic, are not grounds that contributed to the occurrence to the accident and hence no deduction qua contributory negligence is permissible. 
15. In totality of circumstances, this Tribunal is of the opinion that the petitioners have been able to prove at the scales of preponderance of probabilities that the accident in question, took place due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle bearing no. DL-1LAE-4509 by its driver/respondent no.1 on the date and time of accident. Accordingly, issue no.1 is decided in favour of petitioners/claimants and against the respondents. 
Issue no. 2 Whether the injured is entitled to any compensation, if so, to what extent and from whom? OPP. 
16. As regards the issue of liability of the respondents, respondent no.3 has raised a statutory defence pleading that the offending vehicle was being plied in breach of terms and Digitally signed CHARU by CHARU GUPTA GUPTA 04:25:31 Date: 2024.10.21 +0530 MACT No. 326/22 Vidhan Biswas vs. Akendra & 0rs. Page no. 10 of 25(ss) conditions of the insurance policy in as much as the offending vehicle held RC as a goods carriage vehicle and was not permitted to carry victims as passengers. It is further pleaded that since the son of the petitioner no.1 and all other injured victims were mere gratuitous passengers travelling in the offending vehicle without authorization, insurance company is not liable to compensate them. 
Vidhan Biswas (Dar) vs Akendra Kumar (206/21,Lc) on 21 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/62741107/
6 In order to establish this defence, respondent no.3 has examined Sh. Parth Arya, Deputy Manger (legal claims) as R3W1. R3W1 has duly proved the terms and conditions of the insurance policy which clearly do not cover the use of offending vehicle as a passenger vehicle. Since it stands proved in issue no.1 that the offending vehicle was carrying the victims as gratuitous passengers, there is certainly a breach of the terms and conditions of insurance policy. 
Now, whether the payment of compensation is to made jointly by the owner and driver of the vehicle or by the insurer which could thereafter be recovered by the owner and driver, has to be considered in the light of the decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court in Anu Bhanvara vs. IFFCO Tokio General Insurance Company AIR 2019 SC 3934. In the said judgment, Apex Court held that the insurance of the vehicle, though as a goods vehicle, is not disputed by the parties. It held that since the claimants were young children who suffered permanent disability on account of the injuries sustained in the accident, the principle of "pay and recover" should be directed to be invoked in the present case. The court accordingly held that the insurance company shall have right to realize the compensation amount from the CHARU Digitally signed by CHARU GUPTA Date: 2024.10.21 GUPTA 04:25:36 +0530 MACT No. 326/22 Vidhan Biswas vs. Akendra & 0rs. Page no. 11 of 25(ss) driver and owner of the vehicle in accordance with the law. 
Reliance is also placed on decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court in Manuara Khatoon vs. Rajesh Kumar Singh AIR 2017 SC 1204, wherein the court while referring to the case of Manager, National Insurance company Ltd. vs. Saju P. Paul & anr. (2013) 2SCC observed in para "...16. This question also fell for consideration recently in Manager, National Insurance Company Limited vs. Saju P.
Paul & Anr., (supra) wherein this Court took note of entire previous case law on the subject mentioned above and examined the question in the context of Section 147 of the Act. While allowing the appeal filed by the Insurance Company by reversing the judgment of the High Court, it was held on facts that since the victim was travelling in offending vehicle as "gratuitous passenger" and hence, the Insurance Company cannot be held liable to suffer the liability arising out of accident on the strength of the insurance policy. However, this Court keeping in view the benevolent object of the Act and other relevant factors arising in the case, issued the directions against the Insurance Company to pay the awarded sum to the claimants and then to recover the said sum from the insured in the same proceedings by applying the principle of "pay and recover". 
17. Justice R.M. Lodha (as His Lordship then was and later became CJI) speaking for the Bench held in paras 20 and 26 as under:
"20. The next question that arises for consideration is whether in the peculiar facts of this case a direction could be issued to the Insurance Company to first satisfy the awarded amount in favour of the claimant and recover the same from the owner of the vehicle (Respondent 2 herein).
26. The pendency of consideration of the above questions by a larger Bench does not mean that the course that was followed in Baljit Kaur, (2004) 2 SCC 1 and Challa Upendra Rao, (2004) 8 SCC 517 should not be followed, more so in a peculiar fact situation of this case. 17. As regards the quantum of compensation, this court is governed by the law laid down by Hon'le Supreme Court in Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar & Anr. (2011) 1 Supreme Court cases 343, Sarla Verma & Ors. v. Delhi Transport Corporation & Ors. 
(2003) 6SCC 121 and National Insurance Company Limited v. Pranay Sethi & Ors.(2017) 16 SCC 680 . The gist of the law is that the object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner. The court or the Tribunal shall have to assess the damages objectively and exclude from consideration any speculation or fancy, though some conjecture with reference to the nature of disability and its Vidhan Biswas (Dar) vs Akendra Kumar (206/21,Lc) on 21 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/62741107/
8 consequences, is inevitable. A person is not only to be compensated for the physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury. This means that he is to be compensated for his inability to lead a full life, his inability to enjoy those normal amenities which he would have enjoyed but for the injuries, and his inability to earn as much as he used to earn or could have earned. 
18. Further it can be noted that the heads under which compensation is awarded in personal injury cases are the following:
Pecuniary damages (Special damages)
(i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization, medicines, transportation,
nourishing food, and miscellaneous expenditure. 
 (ii) Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the injured Digitally signe  CHARU by CHARU  GUPTA  GUPTA 04:25:52  Date: 2024.10.21 MACT No. 326/22 Vidhan Biswas vs. Akendra & 0rs. Page no. 14 of 25(ss) 
 +0530 would have made had he not been injured, comprising:
(a) Loss of earning during the period of treatment; 
(b) Loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability. 
(iii) Future medical expenses. 
Non-pecuniary damages (General damages)
(iv) Damages for pain, suffering and trauma as a consequence of the injuries.
(v) Loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage). 
(vi) Loss of expectation of life (shortening of normal longevity).
18.1. In routine personal injury cases, compensation will be awarded only under heads (i), (ii) (a)
and (iv). 18.2. It is only in serious cases of injury, where there is specific medical evidence corroborating the evidence of the claimant, that compensation will be granted under any of the heads (ii)(b), (iii),
(v) and (vi) relating to loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability, future medical expenses, loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage) and loss of expectation of life.

18.4. Award under the head of future medical expenses--Item (iii)--depends upon specific medical evidence regarding need for further treatment and cost thereof.

18.6. It was observed by Hon'ble Sc in such case of Raj Kumar (supra) that what usually poses some difficulty is the assessment of the loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability --Item (ii) (a).
18.7. We are not concerned with assessment regarding loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability in this case, as petitioner did not suffer any permanent disability. 
19. As per record Adhar Card of petitioner is Mark B and his PAN Card is Mark C, both of which show his date of birth as 09.03.1995. Accordingly, at the time of accident, his age would be 26 years. 
However, as per MLC Ex.PW1/1, age of victim is noted as 28 years. There is nothing on record to disbelieve or show any apparent forgery in the ID proof filed by the petitioner. As such, age of the petitioner is taken as 26 years. 
20. As per discharge summary Ex.PW1/1 and MLC, victim/injured suffered left ankle fracture of mandible, DER#, distal ulnar#left. He remained hospitalized from 08.11.2021 till 13.11.2021. He has not proved his educational qualifications meaning thereby that the petitioner would have been working only as a unskilled labour on daily wages. Even as per the guidelines issued by this Court Court, long term fixed deposit of amount of compensation is mandatory only in the case of minors, illiterate claimants and widows.
In the case of illiterate claimants, the Tribunal is allowed to consider the request for lumpsum payment for effecting purchase of any movable property such as agricultural implements, rickshaws etc. to earn a living.
In the case of semi-illiterate claimants, the Tribunal should ordinarily invest the amount of compensation in long term fixed deposit.
But if the Tribunal is satisfied for reasons to be stated in writing that the whole or part of the amount is required for expanding an existing business or for purchasing some property for earning a livelihood, the Tribunal can release the whole or part of the amount of compensation to the claimant provided the Tribunal will ensure that the amount is invested for the purpose for which it is demanded and paid.
In the case of literate persons, it is not mandatory to invest the amount of compensation in long term fixed deposit.
Moreover, in the case of literate persons, the Tribunal may resort to the procedure indicated in guideline No. (i) only if, having regard to the age, fiscal background and strata of the society to which the claimant belongs and such other considerations, the Tribunal thinks that in the larger interest of the claimant and with a view to ensure the safety of the compensation awarded, it is necessary to invest the amount of compensation in long term fixed deposit.

Thus, sufficient discretion has been given to the Tribunal not to insist on investment of the compensation amount in long term fixed deposit and to release even the whole amount in the case of literate persons.
However, the Tribunals are often taking a very rigid stand and are mechanically ordering in almost all cases that the amount of compensation shall be invested in long term fixed deposit.
The guidelines were not to be understood to mean that the Tribunals were to take a rigid stand while considering an application seeking release of the money.

The guidelines cast a responsibility on the Tribunals to pass appropriate orders after examining each case on its own merits.
Even in the case of literate persons, the Tribunals are automatically ordering investment of the amount of compensation in long term fixed deposit without recording that having regard to the age or fiscal background or the strata of the society to which the claimant belongs or such other considerations,
the Tribunal thinks it necessary to direct such investment in the larger interests of the claimant and with a view to ensure the safety of the compensation awarded to him.
